source_text: X. Iam nunc, dilectissimi fratres, et de amore quem in nos invicem habemus aliqua dicenda sunt. nec instruimus, sed admonemus quia, sicut simul unanimes fuimus, ita et apud dominum una vivimus et oramus. tenenda est concordia caritatis, dilectionis vinculis inhaerendum est. tunc diabolus prosternitur, tunc a domino quicquid postulatur accipitur, ipso pollicente ac dicente: Si duo ex vobis convenerint super terram de omni re quamcumque petieritis a patre meo, continget vobis. nec alio modo vitam aeternam accipere et cum Christo regnare poterimus, nisi fecerimus quod praecipit faciendum, qui et vitam promisit et regnum. eos denique hereditatem dei consequi, qui pacem cum fratribus tenuerint, suo magisterio ipse dominus denuntiat dicens: Beati pacifici, quoniam filii dei vocabuntur. quod exponens apostolus ait: Sumus filii dei. si autem filii, et heredes; heredes quidem dei, coheredes autem Christi, siquidem compatiamur, ut et commagnificemur. si heres esse non potest nisi filius, filius autem non est nisi pacificus, hereditatem dei habere non poterit qui pacem dei rumpit. et hoc non quasi (non) admoniti dicimus aut sine divina ostensione suggerimus.
pass_a_gloss: Now at this point, most beloved brothers, some things are to be said also about the love which we have among ourselves toward one another. We do not give first instruction, but we give reminder, because just as we have been together of one mind, so also before the Lord we live as one and pray as one. The concord of charity is to be held fast, clinging is to be done to the bonds of affection. Then the devil is thrown down, then whatever is requested from the Lord is received, with himself promising and saying: If two of you shall agree upon earth concerning every matter whatever you shall ask from my Father, it shall come to pass for you. Nor in another way shall we be able to receive eternal life and to reign with Christ, unless we shall have done what he who both promised life and kingdom commands to be done. Finally by his own teaching the Lord himself announces that they attain the inheritance of God who shall have kept peace with the brothers, saying: Blessed peacemakers, because they shall be called sons of God. Explaining which thing the apostle says: We are sons of God. But if sons, also heirs; heirs indeed of God, but co-heirs of Christ, if indeed we suffer together, that we may also be glorified together. If no one can be heir except a son, and no one is a son except a peacemaker, he who breaks the peace of God will not be able to have the inheritance of God. And this we say not as if unadmonished, nor do we urge it without divine manifestation.
pass_b_english: Now, most beloved brothers, I must also say something about the love we have for one another.
I am not instructing you, but reminding you, because as we have stood together of one mind, so before the Lord we live as one and pray as one.
We must hold fast the concord that belongs to charity, and cling to the bonds of affection.

Then the devil is overthrown, and then whatever we ask of the Lord is granted, for he himself promises and says: If two of you agree on earth about anything whatever that you ask of my Father, it shall be done for you (Matthew 18:19).
Nor can we receive eternal life and reign with Christ in any other way, unless we do what he commands to be done, he who promised both life and kingdom.

In his own teaching the Lord himself declares that those who have kept peace with the brethren attain the inheritance of God, saying: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God (Matthew 5:9).

Expounding this, the apostle says: We are sons of God; and if sons, then heirs, heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ, if we suffer with him, so that we may also be glorified with him (Romans 8:16-17).
If no one can be an heir unless he is a son, and no one is a son unless he is a peacemaker, then whoever breaks the peace of God cannot possess the inheritance of God.
And I say this not as one who speaks without admonition, nor do I urge it without divine warrant.

lemmas.gloss: is laid low, of the devil
it shall happen, shall be granted

choices.english: I am not instructing you for the first time, but reminding you
choices.why: present tense first-person plural contrast sets new teaching against reminder of what they already share

choices.english: the concord that belongs to charity, the bonds of affection
choices.why: genitives are descriptive of kind, and parallel nouns require two English nouns rather than collapsing love into one word

choices.term: si quidem compatiamur, ut et commagnificemur
choices.english: if we suffer with him, so that we may also be glorified with him
choices.why: subjunctive protasis with conditional force plus purpose clause gives shared suffering as condition for shared glory
rejected: since we suffer, we shall be magnified
